source.author: José Raúl Capablanca
source.section: Chapter II, §11 Obtaining a Passed Pawn, Example 24

steps.title: Three against three
steps.source: When three or more Pawns are opposed to each other in some such position, there is always a chance for one side or the other of obtaining a passed Pawn. In the following position the way of obtaining a passed Pawn is to advance the centre Pawn.

narration.say: Three pawns against three, with the kings far away.
White can obtain a passed pawn by advancing the centre pawn. Your move.

feedback.*: Push the pawn in the middle of the three.

exercise.prompt: White to move. Break through with the centre pawn.
exercise.wrong: Push the pawn in the middle of the three.
exercise.success: 1. b6. If cxb6, then a6 and the a-pawn is through. So Black plays axb6.

feedback.a6: Black simply takes: bxa6. First c6, to draw the black pawns away.

exercise.prompt: White to move. Give up another pawn.

feedback.*: Not the move Capablanca shows here. Try again.

exercise.success: 3. a6. This white pawn is nearer to queening than any black pawn. White wins.

steps.title: If Black moves first
steps.source: It would not be advisable to try to obtain a passed Pawn because the White Pawns would be nearer to Queen than the single Black Pawn. […] The game properly played would be a draw.

narration.say: If Black has the move, he should not try the same trick: the white pawns are nearer to queening.
Instead, Black plays b6, and the pawns are exchanged.
Properly played, the game is a draw.
